query: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, what is the punishment for tampering with computer source documents?
expected_evidence: Section 65 (Tampering with computer source documents): knowingly or intentionally concealing, destroying or altering computer source code required by law to be kept or maintained is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to two lakh rupees, or both; includes an Explanation defining 'computer source code'.

query: What is the punishment under the IT Act, 2000 for identity theft by using another person's electronic signature or password?
expected_evidence: Section 66C (Punishment for identity theft): fraudulently or dishonestly making use of another person's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine up to one lakh rupees.

query: What does Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provide for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form?
expected_evidence: Section 67: publishing or transmitting lascivious or prurient material in electronic form is punishable on first conviction with imprisonment up to three years and fine up to five lakh rupees, with enhanced punishment on a subsequent conviction.

query: Under Section 72 of the IT Act, 2000, what is the penalty for disclosing secured electronic records or information without the concerned person's consent?
expected_evidence: Section 72: a person who has secured access to any electronic record, book, register, correspondence or information under the Act and discloses it without the consent of the person concerned is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.

query: When is an intermediary exempt from liability for third-party information under Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000?
expected_evidence: Section 79(1): subject to the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3), an intermediary shall not be liable for any third-party information, data or communication link made available or hosted by him.

query: What does Article 14 of the Constitution of India provide regarding equality before the law?
expected_evidence: Article 14: the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

query: Which fundamental right of the Constitution guarantees freedom of speech and expression?
expected_evidence: Article 19 heading (Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.) together with clause 19(1)(a), which guarantees the right 'to freedom of speech and expression'.

query: What does Article 21 of the Constitution guarantee about life and personal liberty?
expected_evidence: Article 21: no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law (the same chunk also contains Article 21A on the right to education).

query: What protection does Article 22 of the Constitution provide to a person who has been arrested?
expected_evidence: Article 22(1): an arrested person shall be informed as soon as may be of the grounds of arrest and shall not be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice.

query: Which Article of the Constitution lays down the procedure for amending the Constitution and what does it require?
expected_evidence: Article 368: Parliament may amend the Constitution by way of addition, variation or repeal of any provision; an amendment is initiated by a Bill in either House and requires a special majority, with ratification by the States required for specified provisions.

query: Can a court grant specific performance of a contract of employment, or declare a wrongfully dismissed employee's service as subsisting?
expected_evidence: Passage holding that a contract of employment is not capable of specific performance and breach cannot found a declaratory judgment of subsistence of employment; such a declaration is not permissible under the Specific Relief Act, though reinstatement may be available under Industrial Law as a special exception.

query: Does a fresh cause of action arise under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act each time a dishonoured cheque is presented again?
expected_evidence: Discussion of MSR Leathers overruling Sadanandan Bhadran: a fresh cause of action within the meaning of Section 142(b) read with Section 138 is deemed to arise every time the cheque is presented and dishonoured and the drawer fails to pay within the period in the proviso to Section 138, so prosecution based on second or successive dishonour is permissible.

query: What categories of cases may justify quashing criminal proceedings in the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure?
expected_evidence: Lists illustrative categories (a), (b), ... in which the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent power under Section 482 CrPC may be exercised to prevent abuse of the process of court or to secure the ends of justice, for example where the FIR/complaint allegations even taken at face value do not constitute an offence.

query: Is registration of an FIR necessary before a court can entertain an application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC?
expected_evidence: Passage stating that registration of a case and entries in the case diary are not necessary for entertaining an application for grant of anticipatory bail; the mere imminence of a likely arrest on a reasonable belief of having committed a non-bailable offence is sufficient to invoke Section 438.

query: What are the essential ingredients required to establish the offence of dowry death under Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code?
expected_evidence: Quotes Section 304B(1): the death of a woman caused by burns or bodily injury, or occurring otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, where it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relative for or in connection with a demand for dowry; punishable with a minimum of seven years extending to life.

query: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, what is the punishment for dishonestly receiving or retaining a stolen computer resource or communication device?
expected_evidence: Section 66B (Punishment for dishonestly receiving stolen computer resource or communication device): whoever dishonestly receives or retains a stolen computer resource or communication device, knowing or having reason to believe it to be stolen, is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.

query: What is the punishment under the IT Act, 2000 for cheating by personation by using a computer resource (Section 66D)?
expected_evidence: Section 66D: whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personation is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine up to one lakh rupees.

query: How does the IT Act, 2000 punish a person who intentionally captures or publishes the image of a private area of another person without consent (violation of privacy)?
expected_evidence: Section 66E (Punishment for violation of privacy): intentionally or knowingly capturing, publishing or transmitting the image of a private area of a person without consent, under circumstances violating privacy, is punishable with imprisonment up to three years or fine up to two lakh rupees, or both.

query: What is the punishment under Section 67A of the IT Act, 2000 for publishing or transmitting material containing a sexually explicit act in electronic form?
expected_evidence: Section 67A: publishing or transmitting material containing a sexually explicit act in electronic form is punishable on first conviction with imprisonment up to five years and fine up to ten lakh rupees, and on second or subsequent conviction with imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to ten lakh rupees.

query: What does Section 67C of the IT Act, 2000 require of intermediaries regarding preservation and retention of information?
expected_evidence: Section 67C(1): an intermediary shall preserve and retain such information for such duration and in such manner and format as the Central Government may prescribe.

query: What does Article 15 of the Constitution prohibit regarding discrimination against citizens?
expected_evidence: Article 15(1): the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.

query: What does Article 16 of the Constitution provide about equality of opportunity in matters of public employment?
expected_evidence: Article 16(1): there shall be equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.

query: What does Article 23 of the Constitution prohibit with regard to human trafficking and forced labour?
expected_evidence: Article 23(1): traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited, and any contravention is an offence punishable in accordance with law.

query: What does Article 25 of the Constitution guarantee regarding freedom of conscience and religion?
expected_evidence: Article 25(1): subject to public order, morality and health and the other provisions of Part III, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practice and propagate religion.

query: What right does Article 30 of the Constitution confer on minorities in relation to educational institutions?
expected_evidence: Article 30(1): all minorities, whether based on religion or language, have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

query: In a case resting on circumstantial evidence, how complete must the chain of incriminating circumstances be before a conviction can be recorded?
expected_evidence: Passage stating that where conviction is based on circumstantial evidence the chain of incriminating circumstances must be so complete that the innocence of the accused is incompatible with it and it must lead only to the guilt of the accused.

query: Does the rule of res judicata under Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure apply to petitions filed under Article 32 of the Constitution?
expected_evidence: Passage holding that res judicata, though it has some technical aspects, is founded on public policy (finality of decisions and avoiding vexing a party twice) and cannot be treated as irrelevant in dealing with petitions under Article 32.

query: Can an arbitral award be set aside merely on a general allegation that the arbitral tribunal did not consider certain documents?
expected_evidence: Passage holding that a mere general statement that documents were not considered is not a ground to set aside an arbitral award; the party must show what the document was, when it was filed, its relevance, the impact had it been considered, and how its non-consideration rendered the award patently illegal.

query: On whom does the burden of proof lie to establish a breach of policy conditions when an insurer seeks to avoid liability?
expected_evidence: Passage holding that to avoid liability the insurer must prove the insured was guilty of negligence / failed to fulfil the policy condition (e.g., use of the vehicle by a duly licensed driver), and that the burden of proving breach lies on the insurer.

query: Can a conviction be based on a dying declaration even without corroboration?
expected_evidence: Passage noting that a dying declaration is admissible in evidence and a conviction can be recorded on it without corroboration, though the circumstances in which it was recorded may be scrutinised to test its genuineness.
